data.note: prose-pin coverage check before editing an instruction file

data.claim: Harvesting every non-docstring string literal (>=12 chars) from the Python test suite, and matching it whitespace-flattened and case-folded against the flattened document, finds every hand-written prose pin in this repo's suites for the shipped instruction files. Leftover noise only marks more text as pinned, which is the safe direction.
data.falsifier: A needle that tests/test_implement_command.py pins in implement.md or implement-phase.md is not reported, or the pinned fraction is implausibly high (most of the document), so the report cannot tell free text from held text.
data.mechanism: Prose pins in this repo (and in adopting projects) are `assert "<needle>" in text` or parametrize lists of needles; both are ast.Constant str nodes (f-string constant parts too), so an AST walk finds them without knowing the helper's name. That avoids the alias, parametrize and module-list resolution bugs the source project's pin()-callee matcher went through (roborev 558/577/629).
data.probe_output: implement.md 7869 flattened bytes, pinned 512, needles 27: includes all 5 parametrized pins of test_implement_command.py ('exactly FOUR cases', 'never a terminal stop', 'disarm it before any deliberate stop', 'Termination checklist', 'ddflow_recover') plus 'No scope was named', 'Do not ask which'. implement-phase.md 9775 B, pinned 582, 31 needles: includes "No\nreviewer sees another's verdict" (whitespace-flattened), 'may never **promote**', 'wait for every one to report', '`implement` workflow command'. AGENTS.md 2481 B pinned 271. Noise: tool-name literals like 'ddflow_brief' (test_api_layer.py maps) also count as pins; this only errs toward pinned.
data.question: Can ddflow report which text of an instruction file a test suite pins, for a project that has no dedicated pin() helper?

ddflow pins --min-needle 0 / ddflow_pins min_needle=0 silently becomes the default 12 (0 doubles as 'unset'), so an explicitly lowered floor reports short pinned text FREE (rubber-duck, CONFIRMED by probe)

data.rule: When a numeric or string option has a default, represent 'not given' as None on every surface (argparse default=None, MCP a.get(k) is None) and validate the explicit value; `x or DEFAULT` silently turns an explicit 0/'' into the default, and in a safety tool that flips the answer in the unsafe direction.
data.title: Never let 0 (or "") mean both 'unset' and a real value: use None for unset
